operation.source_intent: Persist the tenant-owned site profile, verify the real WordPress REST boundary, persist protected WordPress credentials only after successful verification, clear browser credential material, and then start the tenant-aware initial synchronization

security.site_identity: server-created; caller-owned tenant_id, site_id, actor_user_id, status and other unexpected fields are rejected
security.credential_storage: SiteCredential secret_value encrypted cast only after successful WordPress verification; failed verification stores no credential; secret never returned by API
security.browser_secret_policy: Application Password state is cleared after submission and never echoed in rendered authoritative state
security.csrf: mutation is on the Laravel web/auth/tenant.context route stack and frontend apiRequest supplies the CSRF token
security.initial_sync_gate: SyncRun and SyncSiteJob are created/dispatched only after successful WordPress verification
security.idempotency: tenant-scoped Idempotency-Key receipt rejects conflicting payloads and replays terminal outcomes; a new-key credential retry reuses the active-tenant site profile by URL and updates the encrypted credential without duplicating the site or sync run
security.audit: immutable tenant-scoped AuditEvent records credential persistence and verified queue/failure milestones without secrets

coverage: exact canonical operation identity and mutation route
credential non-persistence on failed verification plus encrypted persistence and secret non-exposure on success
no initial synchronization before verification success
tenant-aware queued initial synchronization after verification
idempotent replay without duplicate site, credential or sync run
authoritative persisted site, verification and sync reread
browser Application Password clearing after submission
failed connection retry with a new idempotency key reuses the same tenant-owned site and credential
